title: Part Time Property & Finance Officer
description:
Venn Group are delighted to be partnering with a leading community-focused organisation in the recruitment of a Temporary Part time Property & Finance Officer. This is an excellent opportunity to join a diverse and purpose-driven organisation that manages a substantial mixed-use estate, supporting a wide range of tenants, community groups and local stakeholders. Working closely with the Finance and Property teams, you will support the management of property-related income and financial transactions, ensuring accurate financial records and excellent service delivery to tenants.

Key Responsibilities:
- Maintain tenancy and charging information within the property management system
- Raise and issue rent demands, ensuring accurate posting of transactions to financial ledgers
- Manage credit control activities, following up on outstanding debts via phone, email and written correspondence
- Maintain and reconcile tenant debtor accounts and rental ledgers
- Process expenditure postings to service charge accounts and support monthly reconciliations
- Prepare and post tenancy-related journals, including rent adjustments and recharges
- Review void properties and tenant recharges, ensuring accurate accounting records
- Assist with month-end reporting and financial administration activities
- Work collaboratively with colleagues across Finance and Property teams
- Support the delivery of accurate financial procedures, controls and reporting

Ideal Candidate Profile:
- Previous experience within a rental accounting, property finance or income accounting environment
- Experience using computerised accounting systems
- Strong Excel skills and confidence manipulating financial data and reports
- Excellent attention to detail with strong data entry and reconciliation skills
- Strong organisational, analytical and administrative abilities
- Effective written and verbal communication skills
- Proven ability to follow financial procedures and controls accurately
- Proactive, resourceful and flexible approach to work
- Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment
- AAT/CAT studies or qualification would be advantageous
- Experience of property management systems, rental ledgers and credit control would be highly desirable

Role: Part Time Property & Finance Officer

Contract: 3 month contract with chance to extend

Location: West London

Working Pattern: Office-based, 3 days per week

Hours: 21 hours per week (Monday to Wednesday)

Job Reference: J97863

To discuss this opportunity in more detail, please contact Venn Group for a confidential conversation or submit your application today.

Venn Group is an equal opportunities employment business and employment agency and welcomes applications from all candidates.

title: Finance and Operations Assistant
description:
The organisation

You'll join a small property business offering broad exposure across several real estate investment and development companies. The role provides part-time flexibility and the opportunity to develop as your responsibilities grow.

The role and responsibilities

Reporting directly to the Financial Controller, the Property Finance and Operations Assistant will:

Raise rent and service charge demands and manage credit control.

Process invoices, expenses, payments and utility recharges.

Complete bank reconciliations and maintain cashflow records.

Maintain sales and purchase ledgers using Propman.

Support quarter-end processes, VAT preparation and service charge reconciliations.

Assist with Charity Trust administration and donations.

Support the smooth running of the office, including systems, suppliers, records and correspondence.

The skills needed

The successful Property Finance and Operations Assistant will have:

Working knowledge of similar finance and administrative responsibilities.

A sound understanding of basic accounting and double-entry bookkeeping.

Good attention to detail and communication skills.

Working knowledge of Microsoft Office or Google Workspace.

The ability to prioritise workloads and work independently within a small team.

Property-sector experience, Propman knowledge and an AAT or similar qualification are desirable rather than essential.

This is an opportunity for a Property Finance and Operations Assistant seeking a broad part-time role with direct exposure to the Financial Controller and room to develop.

Interviews are ongoing, so apply now to be considered.

title: Finance Manager (part-time)
description:
Finance Manager - Overview

We are recruiting a part-time Finance Manager to join an independent Creative Agency based in Central London. You'll join a close-knit team and work with the fractional Finance Director, overseeing AP, AR, management accounts, cashflow and project costing.

This role offers excellent autonomy and flexibility, part-time 3dpw with hybrid working available

Finance Manager - The Role
- Accounts Payable & Receivable: Manage supplier payments, freelancer fees, expenses, credit cards, sales invoicing, receipts and credit control.
- Management Accounts: Produce monthly management accounts, reconciliations, month-end journals, shoot project accounting and VAT returns.
- Cashflow Forecasting: Maintain weekly rolling cashflow forecasts, identify pinch points and plan payment schedules.
- General Finance: Coordinate payroll/pensions, maintain the system and continuously improve financial controls.

Finance Manager - The Person
- Prior experience in a creative, agency or media business.
- Finance qualification not essential.
- Strong end-to-end ledger management, management accounts and cashflow forecasting skills.
- Proficiency in Xero and project accounting is desirable.
- Excellent communication, organisation and attention to detail.

Due to the high volume of applications, only candidates with relevant finance experience will be contacted. If you do not hear from us, please consider your application unsuccessful on this occasion, but we encourage you to apply for future opportunities.

title: Company Secretary Assistant
description:
Company Secretarial Assistant

We're working with a FTSE 250 organisation that is expanding its Company Secretarial team and is looking for a Company Secretarial Assistant. This is a brilliant opportunity to develop your technical knowledge, gain exposure to a diverse client portfolio, and grow your career within a fast-paced, ambitious business that's committed to excellence in governance.

Perks
- Salary- £40-50k depending on experience
- London City Office
- Performance-based bonus
- Generous employer pension contributions
- Private healthcare cover
- Health cash plan
- Life assurance
- Buy/sell annual leave scheme
- Structured development pathway with opportunities for progression

What You'll Be Doing

Key responsibilities include:
- Conduct thorough reviews of company secretarial work, including board minutes and resolutions, shareholder resolutions and statutory filings, ensuring accuracy, completeness and compliance with legal and regulatory requirements
- Monitor adherence to internal processes, standards and best practices, identifying any gaps or inconsistencies
- Ensure that all statutory filings comply with the Companies Act and other relevant laws and regulations
- Maintain oversight of electronic corporate records using Diligent Entities to ensure data integrity and regulatory compliance and undertake any statutory filings with the Registrar of Companies
- Work closely with team members to provide feedback on their work, identifying opportunities for improvement and ensuring high-quality service delivery
- Support the development of standardised templates, guidance notes and best practice frameworks to enhance efficiency and accuracy in corporate secretarial processes
- Contribute to the development and refinement of internal procedures, ensuring they align with evolving legal and regulatory requirements
- Provide coaching and training to team members on quality standards, governance requirements and best practices in company secretarial work
- Provide advice on corporate governance best practice and reviewing relevant documentation
- Support professional development by sharing insights and feedback to enhance technical knowledge and skill levels within the team
- Conduct periodic reviews and refresher sessions to reinforce key compliance and quality expectations
- Support the development of quality assurance reporting metrics to track performance and areas for improvement

About You

We're looking for an enthusiastic, proactive professional who is keen to grow within the company secretarial field.

You will ideally:
- Be CGI part or fully qualified (or other professional qualification if relevant experience can be demonstrated)
- Enjoy collaborating with peers and sharing knowledge
- Pro-actively request and act upon feedback received on the quality of work produced

Interested? Let's talk.

If you're ready to join a respected FTSE 250 company where you'll be supported to learn, grow and make a real impact, do reach out. This role won't be around for long, so don't delay - apply today!

title: Patent Secretary
description:
Patent Secretary - London

A leading IP firm is looking to appoint a Patent Secretary to support its growing London based biotech team. The firm offers a collaborative working environment, a varied workload and the opportunity to develop your knowledge across a broad range of patent work. With a strong benefits package and a 35 hour working week, this is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build a long term career within IP.

The successful candidate will provide day to day secretarial and administrative support to the patent team, working closely with attorneys and other colleagues. The role offers variety across patent applications, formalities, billing, document preparation and general team support, with training provided on specialist systems where required.

Responsibilities
- Drafting and formatting letters and emails
- Making amendments to patent specifications using Track Changes
- Preparing forms and documentation for new patent applications
- Preparing legal documents, including extension of time requests
- Supporting online patent filings
- Using patent databases and Patent Office websites to locate and download specifications and correspondence
- Preparing internal memos, forms and other documentation
- Handling internal queries and telephone calls
- Assisting with billing and entering time and disbursements
- Preparing documents for hearings
- Producing reports from the firm's CRM system
- Attending team meetings and providing occasional minute taking support
- Providing audio and copy typing support when required
- Taking on additional responsibilities as required

Requirements
- Previous experience within a patent, legal or professional services environment
- Strong knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel and Outlook
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities
- A proactive, practical and willing approach to learning
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team
- Strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with colleagues at all levels
- Comfortable working under pressure and remaining calm in demanding situations
- Flexible approach to responsibilities and working requirements

title: Credit Controller
description:
Role: Experience Credit Controller

Reporting to: Finance Manager

Location: London, N18 3 BH

Job Type: Full-time

Our client is looking for an experienced and proactive Credit Controller to join their Finance Department. The successful candidate will take responsibility for managing customer accounts, controlling credit exposure, collecting outstanding debts and ensuring customer accounts and payment allocations are accurate and up to date. The role requires close coordination with the Billing Department and regular reporting to the Finance Manager and Finance Director on collections and expected cash receipts for cash-flow planning.

Main Duties
- Proactively manage the sales ledger and collect outstanding customer debts by telephone and email.
- Monitor live customer balances, credit limits and credit utilisation daily.
- Contact customers approaching their credit limits and provide statements where required.
- Place customers exceeding their approved credit limit or payment terms on stop, and remove accounts from stop promptly once payment has been received and allocated.
- Communicate account stop/release information to the relevant operational departments.
- Contact customers before invoices become due to confirm invoices have been received, are correct and are approved for payment.
- Work closely with the Billing Department to resolve missing invoices, invoice queries and disputes promptly so that payments are not unnecessarily delayed.
- Maintain accurate expected payment dates and collection notes and provide the Finance Manager and Finance Director with regular updates on collections and expected cash receipts.
- Maintain and regularly review the aged debtor report, identifying overdue, disputed and high-risk accounts.
- Allocate customer receipts accurately to Sage, including BACS, cheque and credit-card payments.
- Reconcile daily credit-card transactions and receipts against payment-provider reports, the invoicing system and bank receipts.
- Maintain credit-card reconciliation records and investigate any differences promptly.
- Process and reconcile non-account/customer card transactions and related invoices, ensuring payments and invoices are correctly matched and recorded.
- Produce and issue customer statements and overdue-payment correspondence.
- Process credit-note requests, ensuring the correct supporting information and approval is obtained before credit notes are raised and issued.
- Record disputed invoices accurately and coordinate with Billing to ensure disputes are investigated and resolved.
- Evaluate new credit applications and carry out credit checks using Credit Reference Agencies.
- Maintain approved customer credit limits and payment terms.
- Complete regular reconciliations between Sage 50 Accounts Professional, Waste Logic and other relevant payment/invoicing systems.
- Deal promptly with customer account queries and manage the Credit Control mailbox.
- Ensure customer accounts, payment allocations, credit-control notes and supporting records remain accurate and fully up to date.

Experience & Skills

The successful candidate should have strong previous Credit Control experience and be confident managing a busy debtor ledger, chasing payments and dealing directly with customers. Experience of payment allocation, credit-card reconciliation, aged debt management, credit limits, account stops, customer reconciliations and invoice disputes is important.

The candidate must be proactive, organised and confident communicating with customers and internal departments. Strong attention to detail and reconciliation skills are essential. Experience using Sage 50 Accounts Professional is highly desirable, and experience with Waste Logic or similar waste-management/invoicing software would be an advantage. Previous experience within the construction, recycling, waste management or haulage industry would also be advantageous.

- Business partnering: Lead financial review meetings with Heads of Service, discussing income performance, outstanding debt and agreed actions.

description: Medical Receptionist GP Practice Working days/hours: Monday -14.00pm - 18.30pm Wednesday - 14.00pm - 18.30pm Thursday - 13.00pm - 18.00pm Friday -14.00pm - 18.30pm We are looking for a friendly, organised and enthusiastic Medical Receptionist to join our busy GP Practice team. As the first point of contact for our patients, you will play a vital role in delivering a welcoming, professional and efficient service. Your responsibilities will include managing appointments, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, supporting patients with their needs, and carrying out a variety of administrative tasks, including processing clinical correspondence, Docman and eConsult workflows. We are seeking someone with excellent communication skills, a caring and compassionate approach, and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment. Why join us? You will become part of a supportive and dedicated team where your contribution is valued, and where you can make a real difference to patients and the local community every day. Provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception service to patients and visitors. Manage patient appointments, registrations and general enquiries, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Identify and appropriately direct urgent patient requests in accordance with Practice procedures. Handle incoming calls, messages and home visit requests, liaising with clinical staff as required. Undertake general administrative duties, including processing clinical tasks, correspondence, Docman and eConsult workflows. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records, including data entry, scanning and filing documentation. Process payments for private services and issue receipts where required. Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with Practice policies, data protection and safeguarding requirements. Support the wider Practice team to ensure the smooth running of daily operations and delivery of high-quality patient care. Maintain a clean, tidy and welcoming reception and waiting room environment. Key Responsibilities 1. Reception and Patient Services Provide a welcoming, courteous and efficient reception service to patients and visitors. Respond to patient enquiries in person and over the telephone, providing accurate information and assistance. Book, amend and cancel appointments, including new and follow-up appointments, in accordance with Practice procedures. Use effective communication skills and sound judgement to identify patients requiring urgent attention, ensuring they are directed appropriately without disrupting the smooth running of the Practice. Explain Practice procedures, registration requirements and services to new and temporary patients, ensuring all necessary documentation is completed. 2. Telephone and Communication Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally, directing enquiries to the appropriate person or department. Take accurate messages and ensure they are communicated to the relevant team members in a timely manner. Liaise with the Duty Doctor regarding home visit requests, following Practice protocols. Communicate effectively and sensitively with patients, carers, healthcare professionals and external organisations. Handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and professionalism. 3. Administrative Duties Undertake a range of general administrative duties to support the efficient operation of the Practice. Process clinical and administrative tasks accurately and within agreed timescales. Manage and action Docman correspondence and workflows, ensuring documents are appropriately processed and allocated. Monitor and process eConsult requests in accordance with Practice procedures, escalating clinical concerns to the appropriate team members. Enter and update patient information accurately on the clinical computer system. Scan and attach incoming correspondence and relevant documentation to the correct patient medical records. Support the clinical and administrative teams with other duties as required. 4. Patient Records and Information Management Maintain accurate, complete and up-to-date patient records in accordance with Practice policies. Retrieve, organise and re-file paper medical records where required, ensuring appropriate filing procedures are followed. Ensure patient records and documentation are maintained in good condition and stored securely. Handle all patient information in accordance with confidentiality requirements, UK GDPR and Practice information governance policies. 5. Payments and Private Services Provide patients with information regarding fees for private and non-NHS services. Accept payments, issue receipts and maintain accurate records of transactions in accordance with Practice procedures. 6. Teamwork and General Responsibilities Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, administrative colleagues and the wider Practice team to ensure a high standard of patient service. Support colleagues during busy periods and contribute to the effective day-to-day running of the Practice. Follow all Practice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and control, and confidentiality. Attend relevant training, staff meetings and development activities as required. The successful candidate will be expected to provide cover for thier colleagues during periods of annual leave and sick leave, subject to operational requirements. Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role, as directed by the Practice Manager or the Partners.

title: Reception Administrator
description: We are looking for highly motivated reception administrators to join our dynamic and friendly team to work in state of the art GP Led Health Centre, rated "Outstanding " by CQC, in Pinner which is open 8am-8pm, 7days a week. We are an innovative and forward thinking EMIS practice committed to delivering the highest standard of patient care. Hours are mainly Monday Friday however some weekend cover is also required. Competitive salary offered. To provide and maintain a high standard of care for visaitors and patients as well as providing assistance to other members of the primary healthcare team. The duties will include all tasks normally undertaken by a reception administrator. This will include but is not limited to the following: To ensure that all visitors, telephone callers, and patients accessing the practice are greeted professionally. To ensure all telephone calls are managed appropriately. To assist patients in accessing the most appropriate healthcare professional to meet their clinical need. To manage the flow of patients and patient administration queries. To ensure the administrative clinical pathways are followed. Reception duties: Greeting and booking in or patients for surgeries and clinics. Dealing with patient enquiries efficiently and courteously. The receiving and recording of telephone messages taking appropriate action Making appointments on Emisweb, by processing appointment requests for today, future appointments from patients in person and on the telephone. Dealing with all telephone queries/requests from patients, and acting as liaison with the Doctors/Nurses as necessary. Pulling and filing medical records as necessary. Processing repeat prescriptions and filing for collection within 48 hours. Taking home visit requests Advising patients of relevant charges for private services Receiving specimens from patients ensuring all their details have been recorded whilst following Health & Safety policy. Administration duties: To have a thorough knowledge of all practice policies and procedures To work in accordance of written protocols Provide administrative support for clinical staff. Filing patient records and correspondence when necessary Opening and distribution or practice post. Registering new patients following the Registration Protocol. Scanning of documents onto the medical system. All scanning should be cleared daily. To send letters to patients as necessary. Photocopying of notes and other information (in reception this includes: ensuring enough forms are printed or photocopied: consent forms, appointment card, change of details etc.). Changing details on Emisweb i.e. Change of address, telephone numbers etc. Cover for other team members may be required for sickness and annual leave. To carry out any other duties agreed between employee and the practice to ensure the smooth running of the practice.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for an experienced, friendly and enthusiastic GP Receptionist/Administrator to join our busy, welcoming and supportive team. As the first point of contact for our patients, you will play an important role in providing a professional, caring and efficient service. The role involves a mixture of reception and administrative duties, helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Previous experience working in a GP practice reception role is essential, as we are looking for someone who understands the demands of general practice, can confidently manage a busy reception environment and is familiar with supporting patients in a healthcare setting. We are looking for someone who is organised, reliable, compassionate and a great team player, with excellent communication skills and a positive, can-do attitude. Why join us? We pride ourselves on being a friendly, hardworking and supportive team who genuinely care about our patients and each other. We value everyone's contribution and aim to create a positive working environment where you feel supported, appreciated and part of the team. If you have previous GP reception experience, enjoy working with people and are looking for a rewarding role where no two days are the same, we would love to hear from you! The successful candidate will be responsible for providing a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients and the wider practice team at The Elgin Clinic. Main duties will include welcoming patients, answering telephone calls, booking and cancelling appointments, managing patient enquiries and directing patients to the appropriate healthcare professional or service. The role will also involve processing repeat prescription requests, managing incoming correspondence, scanning and filing documents, updating patient records, handling emails and carrying out general administrative tasks to support the smooth running of the practice. The successful candidate will work closely with GPs, nurses and other members of the practice team, ensuring patient information is handled accurately and confidentially. They must be able to manage a busy workload, prioritise tasks, remain calm under pressure and deal with patients in a caring and professional manner. Previous experience working in a GP reception role is essential, along with good communication, organisational and IT skills. We are looking for a reliable, flexible and enthusiastic team player who is committed to providing excellent patient care. Job Description GP Receptionist/Administrator The Elgin Clinic is looking for an experienced, friendly and motivated GP Receptionist/Administrator to join our busy and supportive practice team. The successful candidate will be responsible for providing an efficient, professional and welcoming service to patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. As an important member of the practice team, you will help ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the surgery while delivering a high standard of patient care. The role involves a combination of reception and administrative responsibilities, including answering telephone calls, booking and managing appointments, dealing with patient enquiries, processing prescription requests and directing patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional or service. Administrative duties will include managing incoming correspondence, scanning and filing clinical documents, updating patient records, processing emails and completing general administrative tasks accurately and efficiently. You will work closely with GPs, nurses, healthcare professionals and other members of the practice team to ensure patients receive a timely, caring and professional service. The successful candidate must be able to manage competing priorities, work effectively under pressure and handle sensitive or challenging situations with patience, empathy and professionalism. Maintaining patient confidentiality and following practice policies and procedures will be essential. Previous experience working in a GP reception role is essential. Applicants should have good IT skills, excellent communication and organisational abilities, and a sound understanding of the demands of working in a busy GP practice. We are looking for someone who is reliable, flexible, proactive and enjoys working as part of a team. At The Elgin Clinic, we value teamwork, mutual support and a positive working environment where everyone contributes to delivering the best possible care to our patients.

title: Receptionist

You will play an important part in ensuring patients are directed to the right services and receive timely, appropriate care. Overall, the GP Receptionist role is vital in supporting high-quality patient care and contributing to the effective running of the NHS GP practice. title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: Pentelow practice is busy practice, located in Feltham. We are in a process of recruiting a receptionist for a total of 27 hours per week . Candidate must be willing to work between 14:00 and 18:30 Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. On Wednesdays, the hours will be 09:00 to 18:30. You will be the first point of contact for members of the public and patients of the practice, along with other medical colleagues so a good communication skill is essential. Also you should have a calm and confident approach in dealing with the general public. Previous working within a GP practice is desired and will add a plus point. Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice. Unlock consulting rooms, switch on computers and lights, Ensure Drs and Nurses room for printer paper, couch rolls and ensure consulting rooms are tidy Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system, sorting out Rotas for the Drs Arrange transport to hospital appointments for housebound patients Register new patients,carefully checking all details for accuracy and enter on computer registration link Processing and distributing incoming and outgoing mail Taking messages and passing on information Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Check Practice Emails, Referrals via ERS System, two week wait audit. Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, Shredding, Deductions, Registrations, photocopying and scanning. Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Cover sickness/annual leave and work reasonable overtime when required, including some weekends. Perform any other relevant and reasonable duties that may be requested by the lead receptionist, practice manager or partners. Undertake all mandatory training as required Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice, including the provision of secretarial and clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies. Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the lead receptionist/practice manager, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Opening up/locking up of practice premises, activation/deactivation of alarm system and maintaining security in accordance with practice/health centre protocols Register new patients, temporary residents and any requiring immediate and necessary treatment, carefully checking all details for accuracy and enter on computer registration link Filing and retrieving paperwork Reconcile new patients notes with relevant FP7s and FP8s Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, Shredding, Deductions, Registrations, photocopying and scanning Undertake all mandatory training as required. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy and the practice infection control policy. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way, free from hazards Actively reporting health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general/patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Demonstrate due regard for safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. PENTELOW PRACTICE Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate This job description should be regarded only as a guideline to the duties required and is not definitive or restrictive in any way and will be reviewed periodically as the practice develops.

title: Service Administrator
company: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
description: This post provides administrative support to the Palliative Care Team based at North Middlesex University Hospital. The post-holder will provide a high-quality administrative service and patient coordination system to the multidisciplinary specialist palliative care team. The post-holder will work within the teams to coordinate the non-clinical aspects of the services including data input and office management support. He / she will need to be able to organise and prioritise their own workload, use initiative and work without constant supervision. The administrator will work across the two services on allocated days and be required to use Careflow and other electronic databases to capture referrals and procedural information. The post holder will be required to: Ordering of all stationaries on Pecos. Ordering of all information leaflets (booklets /forms DWP, CMC). Emailing urgent letters to GP and other professionals Collection and distribution of all post & letters into the department. Update attendance records in excel for MDT. Room bookings/ circulation to team members for meetings. Contact other NHS and private healthcare providers for patient information for emergency admissions and updating with discharge summaries. Ensure all enquiries from other hospitals are effectively managed by being successfully resolved or escalated to the CNS's Ensure all relevant people are informed and an appropriate record is maintained liaising and effectively communicating at all levels using written, oral and electronic methods. Use tact and sensitivity to deal with difficult issues. Request clinical data sets from other healthcare providers hospitals in accordance in a timely manner. The post holder will provide comprehensive administrative and patient coordination support to the multidisciplinary Specialist Palliative Care Team across North Middlesex University Hospital and associated services. The role is essential in ensuring the efficient operation of the service by managing administrative processes, coordinating referrals, maintaining accurate records, and supporting communication between healthcare professionals, patients, carers, and external organisations. The post holder will work independently, prioritising their workload effectively while ensuring high standards of accuracy, confidentiality, and professionalism. They will contribute to the smooth running of the service through effective office management and administrative support. Provide a high-quality administrative service to the Specialist Palliative Care Team. Act as the first point of contact for telephone, email, and face-to-face enquiries, ensuring queries are resolved appropriately or escalated when necessary. Manage incoming and outgoing correspondence, including the collection, distribution, and filing of post and letters. Prepare, format, distribute, and electronically file correspondence, reports, minutes, and other service documentation. Maintain efficient filing systems in accordance with Trust policies and information governance requirements. Organise and coordinate meetings, including room bookings, diary management, preparation and circulation of meeting agendas and papers. Record and maintain attendance registers and multidisciplinary team (MDT) records using Excel and other electronic systems. Order and monitor stationery and departmental supplies using approved procurement systems, including PECOS. Receive, process, and coordinate referrals to the Specialist Palliative Care Team using Careflow and other electronic patient record systems. Ensure accurate and timely data entry of referrals, patient information, and service activity. Track referrals and ensure relevant information is available to clinical staff in a timely manner. Liaise with patients, carers, healthcare professionals, GPs, hospitals, hospices, and community services to facilitate effective communication and coordination of care. Obtain patient information, discharge summaries, and clinical documentation from NHS and independent healthcare providers where required. Request and manage clinical datasets and supporting information from external organisations in accordance with Trust policies and information governance requirements. Communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all levels using telephone, written, and electronic communication methods. Ensure urgent correspondence, including clinical letters and discharge-related communications, is transmitted promptly to GPs and other healthcare professionals. Provide administrative support for multidisciplinary meetings and service activities. Ensure all enquiries from healthcare providers are managed efficiently and escalated appropriately to Clinical Nurse Specialists or other members of the multidisciplinary team when required. Use tact, diplomacy, and sensitivity when dealing with difficult or sensitive situations involving patients, relatives, carers, and professionals. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient and service records on Careflow and other electronic databases. Produce routine reports and activity data as required by the service. Ensure compliance with Trust policies relating to confidentiality, data protection, information governance, and record keeping. Monitor and maintain data quality standards to support service reporting and performance monitoring. Support the day-to-day operational management of the office environment. Ensure information leaflets, patient information booklets, DWP forms, Coordinate My Care (CMC) documents, and other service resources are ordered, maintained, and readily available. Assist with service audits, data collection exercises, and quality improvement initiatives as required. Contribute to the continuous improvement of administrative processes and systems to enhance service efficiency and patient experience. Prioritise and organise workload independently, using initiative and judgement where appropriate. Work flexibly across both Specialist Palliative Care services as required by service need. Adhere to all Trust policies, procedures, and statutory requirements. Participate in mandatory training, appraisal, and personal development activities. Maintain professional standards at all times and contribute positively to the objectives of the Specialist Palliative Care Service.

title: Bank Administrator
description: An opportunity has arisen to join the Kingston and Richmond Autism Service in a bank role as an Administrator within the Neurodevelopmental Service. Based at Hollyfield House, you will have a key role in the effective running of a busy service, with responsibilities including referral management, clinical appointments and supporting clinicians within the service. You will also answer queries about the service and will be confident and willing to communicate with neurodivergent people by telephone and face to face, as required. You will need to be well organised in managing clinic appointments, booking and review systems, and coordinating and sending out reports. You will be well supported and highly valued by the Autism Service and will receive regular supervision. The successful applicant will also provide some administrative support to the Adult ADHD Service, as directed by the service leads. Please apply using the NHS Jobs online system. Your application should explain why you are applying for the post, how you believe you would contribute to working in this setting and demonstrate how you meet the requirements of the person specification. Please be aware that the closing date may be brought forward in the event of a high number of applications. Were looking for someone who Has strong administrative and organisational skills, with excellent attention to detail. Can manage competing priorities and work calmly and efficiently in a busy service. Communicates clearly, sensitively and confidently by telephone, email and face to face. Understands the importance of confidentiality, accurate record keeping and timely information sharing. Works well independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Ideally has previous administrative experience within a neurodevelopmental, mental health or healthcare service. The usual working hours are 9am- 5pm and will be Monday Friday and there is some flexibility on the days the hours are worked. You will be based at Hollyfield Road in Surbiton although you will also need to be able to travel to our other sites as needed. We encourage you to discuss your flexibility needs with us before applying or during the interview process. While we may not be able to meet every request exactly, we promise to fully consider your needs and accommodate them where possible. Please note that flexible working options may vary depending on the role. When completing your application please refer to full Job Description - this can be found under supporting documents.

title: Receptionist / Administrator
description: Receptionist / Administrator Location: Parkview Surgery, 60 West Drayton Road, Uxbridge, UB8 3LA Hours: 16.5 hours per week Reports to: Reception Manager Please complete the attached Job Application Form and email it to k.barton8@nhs.net alongside your application. Applications without a completed form will not be considered. Interviews: Tuesday 10 November. Were looking for an enthusiastic, hardworking and approachable person with a positive attitude and a passion for helping others to join our busy practice. This varied role combines patient-facing reception duties with administrative work, helping patients access care and keeping the practice running smoothly. You'll be a confident communicator who listens carefully, puts patients first and handles difficult conversations with empathy and professionalism. Organised and adaptable, you'll respond to changing priorities and take pride in completing tasks accurately and efficiently. A willingness to learn our systems, follow procedures and act on feedback is essential. You'll join a welcoming team that values collaboration, open communication and initiative, with opportunities to develop your skills and make a difference to patients every day. Eligible employees can join the NHS Pension Scheme , with employee and employer contributions made in accordance with scheme rules. This varied role combines welcoming patients, handling telephone enquiries, booking appointments and processing prescription requests with daily administrative duties, including updating patient records, processing clinical documents and actioning emails. You will help patients access appropriate care and support the smooth running of the practice, working flexibly across reception and administration while maintaining accuracy, confidentiality and a professional, helpful approach. Main responsibilities Patient reception and communication Welcome patients and respond to enquiries in person and by telephone with kindness, patience and professionalism. Listen carefully, explain practice processes clearly and direct patients to the appropriate person or service. Remain calm during difficult conversations, help resolve concerns and seek support when needed. Take accurate messages and pass information promptly to the relevant team member. Communicate effectively with patients, carers, colleagues and external services. Appointments and prescriptions Book and manage appointments in line with practice procedures. Receive and pass on home visit requests appropriately. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice guidelines. Administration and patient records Register new patients and update changes to personal details accurately. Maintain patient records using EMIS Web. Process clinical documents through Docman and EMIS in line with training and written protocols. File correspondence and support recalls for medical reviews. Monitor and action incoming emails, referring queries appropriately. Complete general administrative tasks, including photocopying and emailing. Organise and prioritise allocated work, completing tasks accurately and within required timescales. Teamwork and practice support Work flexibly across reception and administration, adapting to changing priorities. Support colleagues and provide agreed cover for staff absence and annual leave. Follow opening, closing and building security procedures. Keep work areas tidy, safe and organised. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. Professional responsibilities Maintain patient, staff and practice confidentiality at all times. Follow practice policies, written protocols and information governance requirements. Uphold equality, dignity and respect in all interactions. Follow health and safety, infection prevention and safeguarding procedures, reporting concerns promptly. Complete required training and participate in appraisals. Take responsibility for learning practice processes, acting on feedback and maintaining agreed standards. Contribute suggestions and participate in service improvements, practice meetings or audits when required.

title: Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised and proactive Administrator to join our friendly team, providing vital support across inpatient and community services. This is a varied role where you will be the first point of contact for patients, visitors and colleagues, helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of clinical and administrative functions. If you have excellent communication skills, enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, and are confident using Microsoft Office and other IT systems, we would love to hear from you. In return, you'll join a supportive team and play an important role in delivering high-quality patient care and services. Previous Applicants need not apply. Responsible for the day to day administration across intermediate with other members of the team. Responsible for supporting colleagues ensuring work is completed within an agreed timeline. Able to populate reports and collate data on agreed templates This role will act as point of contact for patients and visitors, this will entail being calm, professional and empathetic whilst dealing with potentially sensitive and stressfully situations. This role sits within Ealing Community Partners and will act as point of contact for peers and participate in peer support work. The function of this role is IT based in line with the service objective of being paper light, this will entail fully utilising system one, Microsoft office (including excel and outlook) and other IT equipment such as telephonetics and projectors. The Candidate Pack provides an overview of the key tasks and responsibilities of the role, and the person specification outlines the qualifications, skills, experience and knowledge required. Please view as attached The person specification below is not the full person specification, but outlines the criteria against which your application form will be assessed.

title: Receptionist
description: We are seeking a friendly, organised, reliable and compassionate Receptionist to join our busy NHS GP practice in Southall, serving approximately 5,000 registered patients with a clinical team of 7 GPs. The successful candidate will be the first point of contact for patients, providing a professional, welcoming and efficient reception service. The role involves face-to-face, telephone and online patient enquiries, appointment administration and general administrative duties to support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. The ideal candidate will have excellent communication and customer service skills, a calm and professional manner, and the ability to work effectively in a busy environment while maintaining patient confidentiality and delivering a high standard of care. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and courteous manner. Check patients in for appointments and update their arrival status on the clinical system. Respond to patient enquiries in person, by telephone and through online communication channels. Assist patients with appointment bookings, cancellations and rearrangements in line with practice procedures. Treat all patients with dignity, respect, sensitivity and confidentiality. Communicate effectively with patients from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds. Manage difficult or distressed patients calmly and professionally, escalating concerns when necessary. Ensure patients who require additional assistance are supported appropriately. 2. Telephone and Appointment Management Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally. Handle appointment requests in accordance with practice policies and access procedures. Direct calls to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Take accurate messages and ensure they are passed to the relevant person in a timely manner. Explain practice procedures, appointment arrangements and available services clearly. Recognise when a call may require urgent clinical attention and follow the practice's approved escalation procedures. Never provide clinical advice beyond the receptionist's level of training and authorised responsibilities. Use the practice's clinical computer system, SystmOne, Use the practice's clinical computer system, such as EMIS Web or SystmOne, as applicable. Register patient arrivals and update demographic and contact details in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain accurate electronic records and administrative information. Process incoming and outgoing correspondence as directed. Scan, code or file documents in accordance with practice protocols and staff training. Support the processing of prescription requests, medical records requests and other administrative tasks within the scope of the role. Assist with recalls, patient registrations, appointment lists and other routine administrative work. Ensure all information is recorded accurately and handled securely. Maintain strict patient confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, NHS information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures relating to safeguarding children and adults at risk, escalating concerns promptly to the appropriate person. Maintain awareness of confidentiality when speaking on the telephone or at the reception desk. Verify patient identity and follow the practice's procedures before disclosing information. Report any data breaches, confidentiality concerns or incidents to the Practice Manager promptly. Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, managers and other administrative colleagues. Support the daily running of reception, ensuring the reception area remains organised and professional. Assist with incoming post, emails, document handling and general office duties. Follow practice policies, standard operating procedures and health and safety requirements. Attend staff meetings, training sessions and appraisals as required. Assist colleagues during periods of high demand and provide appropriate cover when required. Undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the role and level of responsibility.

title: Receptionist
description: Earl's Court Medical Centre has an exciting opportunity for a Medical Receptionist to join our welcoming and forward thinking Practice team on a part-time basis. Your normal pattern of working will be Monday - Friday, within the hours of 8am-6:30pm (5 hours per day). Interested applicants must have primary care and SystmOne experience. Key Responsibilities include: Greeting and assisting patients at the reception desk Managing appointments, cancellations and patients enquiries Answering telephone calls and directing queries appropriately Processing repeat prescription requests Supporting the administrative and clinical team with day-to-day tasks Maintaining confidentially and ensuring accurate record- keeping Processing ingoing and outgoing patient records This is a patient facing role that requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and a calm, efficient approach to working in a fast-paced environment. Reception duties: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 72 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. (including computerised practice notes), ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables (including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc.). Premises: Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Make and serve refreshments for meetings, ensure the kitchen is kept clean and tidy and air and tidy the waiting room in turn with other staff. Covering colleagues holiday and sick cover as required. Process incoming and outgoing mail according to practice protocols. Record actions taken in patient record where appropriate or in accordance with practice protocols. Complete other Daily/ Weekly and Monthly core tasks to support to smooth running of the reception area Any other administration duties as necessitated by the needs of the practice. Confidentiality : In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Act as Chaperone when requested by clinician and in accordance with the Chaperone policy. Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with the Practice policies and procedures, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of their own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for their own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality : The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication : The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Receptionist
description: Blackheath Standard PMS are looking for an experienced and reliable receptionist to join our friendly Reception Team. The practice is situated in a pleasant part of Blackheath in South East London with good transport links and local shops. The position is for 22 hours per week over four days, based on a seven week rolling rota. Please note that the rota is variable and you will be working different days over a seven week period. This is based on a 7am start and 12.30pm finish 8am start and 1pm finish, 1pm start and 6pm finish, 1.30pm start with a 7pm finish. This can vary , depending on the needs of the practice during sickness and annual leave. Flexibility is essential. Saturday mornings are part of our enhanced access service and there is the option to work these sessions on a rotation basis. Duties include: Covering reception desk, answering telephone calls, booking appointments via AccuRx triage system, dealing with patient queries, order prescriptions, process admin duties for clinical staff, general administration such as filing and liaising with other health care providers in a professional manner, and processing clinical letters through the Docman system. The duties are variable, depending on what is required on the day. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn. The applicant must have the ability to prioritise workload. Applicants must have the ability to work within a team, have experience of EMIS, AccuRx and Docman and IT skills. Previous experience of working in General Practice is essential, further training will be available for any candidates that show a passion for learning. Job Description Main duties include: Covering reception desk greeting patients and visitors with a professional and friendly manner. Manage the booking system efficiently, signposting patients to the relevant services. Answering incoming calls, respond to queries and manage email correspondence promptly. title: Service Administrator
description: To provide administrative support for the Mental Health Practitioner Service, Health & Wellbeing Coach Service and the Social Prescribing Service. To ensure that all patients referred in are logged and triaged to the appropriate member of each service. To contact patients and provide a service introduction to ensure that expectations are clear. To book initial consultations on behalf of service staff and send reminders to patients. Other agreed administrative tasks as requested and agreed with the service leads, such as meeting notes. To support the Service Leads and H&WB Manager with service reporting, to provide visibility to the GP practices around work done. Responsibilities 1. Referral triage for each service. 2. Booking in and carrying out introduction calls for referrals and sending back inappropriate referrals to referrers. 3. Booking in the initial consultation for each patient with the appropriate service team member. 4. Day to day management and oversight of appointment books, active patient load as well as waiting lists. 5. Sending appointment reminder texts. 6. Oversight of DNAs and focused work on improving the current rates for each service. 7. Manage and oversight of complaints & learning events to ensure a reduction of issues especially around patient bookings. 8. Last minute staff sickness appointment cancellations and communication. 9. Ongoing admin support in the office for team members who travel between many different sites/practices such as letter printing and posting letters to patients. 10. If capacity allows a. Supporting service audit completion b. Uploading compliments to teamnet c. Managing the H&WB Teamnet page d. Supporting at all-staff meetings. e. Helping to organize/attend community events/sessions. 11. Any other reasonable duties required by the Service Leads or Health & Wellbeing Manager in support of the services. This team member would be based in head office at Thomas Wall. Team working Work with the Health & Wellbeing Service Leads and team members. Work with the practice & Sutton PCNs teams to ensure delivery of services and programmes. Actively engage in the performance cycle to identify training and support requirements. Communication The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members as required Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly

The ideal candidate will have proven experience in a similar role for at least 1 years and will be EMIS trained, We are looking for a confident candidate who has an excellent telephone manner and is able to thrive under pressure. Main duties of the job: Your duties will include answering telephone calls , registering patients, prescriptions and general admin within the Practice. There will also be online training . title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: We are looking to recruit a friendly full time and part time GP receptionist/administrator. This will include working morning and evening shifts on rotation. The post requires someone with initiative, enthusiasm, excellent communication skills, empathy with patients and colleagues, well organised, reliable and with a flexible approach to team work. The role involves reception and admin duties both patient facing and over the phone. You will need excellent organisational, communication and interpersonal skills, along with the ability to work as part of a team while managing your own workload The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice, including the provision of secretarial and clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Liaising with hospitals and pharmacy Submitting e-consult lites Processing e-consults and e-consult lites Triaging patients to the appropriate services available. Completing tasks from clinicians Scanning and filling clinical/admin letters. Processing incoming post and emails Forwarding prescriptions to the doctors. description: This position is five day a week (Mon to Fri) on site with no remote working. The trust does not offer visa sponsorship for this post. Tyson West 1 is part of Bethlem Royal Hospital. We offer services for men, aged 18-65, who have acute mental illness and require 24 hour hospital care. Acute illnesses start quickly and have distressing symptoms.We provide care for people who live in the London Borough of Croydon.We offer psychiatric assessment, care and treatment in hospital, which helps to reduce the risk to self and others.Our service brings together teams of health and social care professionals, including nurses, psychologists, OTs, social workers and psychiatrists. This position is five day a week on site with no remote working. We are looking for a highly organised, efficient, flexible and proactive person with excellent communication skills to work in the busy post, and who can balance work demands along with the changing needs of the service. The role requires the post holder to communicate with patients, ward staff and visitors, and to develop collaborative working relationships with colleagues and external agencies.
